Large doors lead to a rutted cart track heading east.
Large doors lead out to green pasture.
Large doors lead out to green pasture.

A trap door conceals a large storage area used to hide the gnomes'
treasures from mountain bandits.  The ladder down has been removed,
however, so there is no way to safely descend.

Rooms.Name: Green Pastures Filled with Yaks
Rooms.Description:
Deep, lushly green pastures roll on for as far as you can see,
providing plenty of forage for the farm's small herd of yaks.  The yaks
always know their way home to the barn, though, when they want their
horns polished or their hair trimmed or combed.

Exits.Description: As far as you can see, the lush pasture continues.
As far as you can see, the lush pasture continues.
A big red barn looks back at you
As far as you can see, the lush pasture continues.

Rooms.Name: Green Pastures Filled with Yaks
Rooms.Description:
Deep, lushly green pastures roll on for as far as you can see,
providing plenty of forage for the farm's small herd of yaks.  The yaks
always know their way home to the barn, though, when they want their
horns polished or their hair trimmed or combed.

Exits.Description: A big red barn stares back at you.
As far as you can see, the lush pasture continues.
As far as you can see, the lush pasture continues.
As far as you can see, the lush pasture continues.

Rooms.Name: Green Pastures Filled with Yaks
Rooms.Description:
Deep, lushly green pastures roll on for as far as you can see,
providing plenty of forage for the farm's small herd of yaks.  The yaks
always know their way home to the barn, though, when they want their
horns polished or their hair trimmed or combed.

Exits.Description: As far as you can see, the lush pasture continues.
A big red barn sits squarely east of you.
As far as you can see, the lush pasture continues.
As far as you can see, the lush pasture continues.

Rooms.Name: Gnomish Treasure
Rooms.Description:
Your last thoughts as you fall into the pit filled with
upward-pointing yak horns had probably best be kept to yourself.

Exits.Description: If you are a REAL goddess, you'll just head right back up.

Rooms.Name: The GnomeDome
Rooms.Description:
For as far as the human eye can see, the magical dome over the
agricultural research station provides shelter from the weather and
privacy from curious eyes.  All around you, small, pointy eared gnomes
with charmingly ugly little faces tend flowers and plants of many odd
varieties.  There appears to be a door leading west.

Exits.Description: The magnificent greenhouse continues south of here.
A small wooden door leads west.

Rooms.Name: Sunflowers
Rooms.Description:
You need some sort of eye covering here, for the light is quite
bright and the heat intense.  Hundreds, maybe even thousands of shining
sunflower faces are turned in your direction, and seem to follow you
wherever you go.

Exits.Description:
A small (gnome-sized) wooden door painted white reflects the sunlight
back at you.

Fields of bright, hot sunflowers line both sides of this path.  Doesn't
look comfortable.

Rooms.Name: Sunflower Path
Rooms.Description:
Walking a long a narrow gap in a field of sunflowers, the heat and
light of the plants beats down upon you like an iron club fresh from the
forge.  The gnomes must all have green thumbs, for these sunflowers are
thriving here.

Exits.Description:
The narrow area between the two fields of sunflowers shines brightly in
their light.
The bright light of the sunflowers dims in the distance.

The narrow area between the two fields of sunflowers shines brightly in
their light.

Rooms.Name: Sunflower Path
Rooms.Description:
The radiant light from both huge fields of sunflowers leaves no place
of shade or shadow.  The sunflowers lift their dark faces to the sun,
bright yellow petals waving with pleasure.  The path between the fields
continues westward for a small distance, coming to a stop at a tall
fence.

Exits.Description: The bright faces of the sunflowers compete with the sun.
The bright fields of sunflowers stop abruptly by a tall fence.

Rooms.Name: Shade Trees
Rooms.Description:
Low, leafy trees spread long branches, inviting you to find shadows
and cool comfort beneath them.  Remnants of cookies and ham sandwiches
beneath some of the trees, and a long rope hanging from one of them hint
that you may have stumbled on a picnic spot.  The path south is blocked
by a stream.

Exits.Description: Bright fields of sunflowers warm you in their heat.
Just how strong are you?  The rope leads up ... up ... up ...

Rooms.Name: The Fence
Rooms.Description:
From north and south of you come the heat and light of a million
sunflowers.  It is always summer in the sunflower field, the cycle of
birth and death appears to have stopped here.  To the west is a very
very tall, white painted fence.  A knothole in the fence is just about
at the level of your eye.

Exits.Description:
Bright fields of sunshine extend for some distance, terminating in an
enormous structure made of some clear substance.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: You can see nothing but dark and cold with no sunshine.

Rooms.Name: Up a Swaying Rope
Rooms.Description:
The thick rope rises up and up and up to where it is tied to a sturdy
branch in what, to a gnome, is a very tall tree.  As you climb the rope
it gently swings to and fro over a narrow but apparently deep stream.
Are you about to get a dunking ?

Exits.Description: Leafy green branches reach for the sky and so does your rope.

The rope is swaying rapidly, and the ground beneath you is replaced by
water and again by ground in such rapid succession you may be sick to
your stomach.

Rooms.Name: Up a Swaying Rope
Rooms.Description:
The thick rope rises up and up and up to where it is tied to a sturdy
branch in what, to a gnome, is a very tall tree.  As you climb the rope
it gently swings to and fro over a narrow but apparently deep stream.
Are you about to get a dunking ?

Exits.Description: Leafy green branches reach for the sky and so does your rope.

The rope is swaying rapidly, and the ground beneath you is replaced by
water and again by ground in such rapid succession you may be sick to
your stomach.

Rooms.Name: Intense Vegetation
Rooms.Description:
A narrow, deep cold stream runs east to west here in a rather lazy
fashion.  It is just a bit too wide to jump over.  A long rope dangles
down from a tree overhead, and to the south, thick vines, thorny bushes
and intense vegetation appear to block your path.

Exits.Description: Intense vegetation and thick, thorny vines block the path south.
A thick rope dangles just over your head.

Rooms.Name: Following a road in the mountains
Rooms.Description:
The mountain road whindles as it leads you through the mountainous
terrain. Make sure you do not slip, a fall would be very disastrous.
There seems to be a slight opening in the mountains east of here,
perhaps it is a little valley. Why don't you have a look ?

Exits.Description: The mountain opens up.
A little road trails off.

Rooms.Name: A little field in the mountains
Rooms.Description:
You have reached a little field placed in the middle of the
mountains.  This looks like a place in harmony. No risk of avalanches.
The grass is green and even a few birds chirp happily in the
surrounding. There is nothing wrong with this picture except the
enormous chasm that opens up the mountain on the east side of the
field. Perhaps you should stay here where you are in guaranteed safety.

Exits.Description: A little house stands on the very verge of falling into the chasm.
A little road trails off.

Rooms.Name: A house at a chasm
Rooms.Description:
Standing directly on the very verge of falling into a huge chasm is a
little house. It looks a bit shabby but it still stands there. This is a
bit strange as two heavy ropes lead away from the house over the chasm
to the other side.

Exits.Description: A little clearing looks rather inviting.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
You now see how very large the chasm is. Very large. And there seems to
be a very strange wind blowing in the chasm. Even if you grew wings it
would not be possible to pass it in that manner. Just forget it.

It leads to another similar house on the other side of the chasm.
Perhaps those ropes can be used to take you over to the other side.

Rooms.Name: Standing in a basket inside a wooden house
Rooms.Description:
Ah, The house is a start on a ropeway over the chasm.
The powerful ropes that go over the chasm will, probably, take you over
safe. But you have to work for it. Incorporated in the bottom of the
basket you are standing in is a treadmill. Walk in the opposite
direction you came and the basket will take you over the chasm. Neat and
simple.  The door has closed behind you, so start walking.

Exits.Description: You are not going this way, especially if you try.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The basket is woven tightly together by the same kind of rope as the
rope that carries you. How the rope weaver was able to get the treadmill
into the floor is beyond your ability to comprehend.
Fascinating. Start walking or you will hang here forever...

Rooms.Name: Hanging in a basket over a chasm
Rooms.Description:
The basket is swaying considerably, mostly due to the fact that you
are or were walking around in it and only a little part due to the fact
that a terrible storm roars just a few feet away from you. It seems that
the basket is protected in some kind of safe pocket. You are still not
over so keep on walking or the wind just might get closer...

Exits.Description: Where you came from and where you are not going.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
There has got to be some kind of magic involved  in this, the wind
roars and your little carriage is almost totally unaffected. Perhaps
this is used as some kind of limitation to how many and what kind of
guests that should be allowed to pass over.

Hmmmmm...
It is deep, so very deep. But was not there something gleaming down
there?

Hmmmmm...

Darkness should not be gleaming. There is definitely something wrong
with this place. That depth need to be further investigated but where
can one descent safely. Not here for sure. Maybe a long ladder would
help...

Rooms.Name: Hanging in a basket over a chasm
Rooms.Description:
The basket is swaying considerably, mostly due to the fact that you
are or were walking around in it and only a little part due to the fact
that a terrible storm roars just a few feet away from you. It seems that
the basket is protected in some kind of safe pocket. You are still not
over so keep on walking or the wind just might get closer...

Exits.Description: Where you came from and where you are not going.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
There has got to be some kind of magic involved in this, the wind roars
and your little carriage is almost totally unaffected. Perhaps this is
used as some kind of limitation to how many and what kind of guests that
should be allowed to pass over.

Rooms.Name: Standing in a basket inside a wooden house
Rooms.Description:
Ah, The house is a start on a ropeway over the chasm.
The powerful ropes that go over the chasm will, probably, take you over
safe. But you have to work for it. Incorporated in the bottom of the
basket you are standing in is a treadmill. Walk in the opposite
direction you came and the basket will take you over the chasm.
Neat and simple.  The door has closed behind you so you better
start walking.

Exits.Description: You are not going this way, especially if you try.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The basket is woven tightly together by the same kind of rope as the
rope that carries you. How the rope weaver was able to get the treadmill
into the floor is beyond your ability to comprehend.
Fascinating. Start walking or you will hang here forever...

Rooms.Name: Back in a house at the chasm edge
Rooms.Description:
The basket comes in inside a house again. Easy as it completely lacks
the walls towards the chasm. How does it manage to stand, mysterious.
Well now you have two options:   Either jump 'ashore' or start walking
on another trip. You have paid for unlimited travel as long as you
ticket lasts so why not take another spin?

Exits.Description: You have to walk this way to get out on the ropeway again.
A relative safety on the ground.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
One gone - three to go. When will this shabby pile of rubble called
house fall down? The world is full of unanswered questions. You did not
even know that I was watching, did you ? ....   Mooaahaahaaaaaaaaaaa !!!

Rooms.Name: Back in a house at the chasm edge
Rooms.Description:

the walls towards the chasm. How does it manage to stand, mysterious.

Rooms.Name: A house at a chasm
Rooms.Description:
You are standing next to a house on the very edge of a huge chasm. It
looks really shabby but it stands, even though two strong ropes seem to
drag it into the open mountain. Around the house is a little grassy
field stuffed in between the huge mountains. A small path trails of east
through the grass.

Exits.Description: A small path trails off towards the mountains.

Rooms.Name: A grassy field in the mountains
Rooms.Description:
You have reached a little field in the mountains, but it does not
look as harmonious as one could think or hope. The grass has some
greyish stuff on it that stains your feet when you touch it and on one
of the sides of the field a huge chasm opens up apparently tearing a
house apart.  A little path leads up into the mountains and west to the
house.

Exits.Description: A little house awaits your arrival to fall into the chasm.
A winding path takes you up, up and up.

Rooms.Name: On a mountain path
Rooms.Description:
The path whindles up and down, up and down, but it looks used. You see
the fine grain dust that covers the path. There have to be some places
that this path connects. Keep walking in either direction and you just
might get there. Below you a little field opens up on the mountainside
while the path continues north into a more mountainous terrain.

Exits.Description: A little path takes you through the mountains.
A small field in the mountains awaits your presence.

Rooms.Name: On a mountain path
Rooms.Description:
The path winds up and down, up and down, but it looks used. You see
the fine grain dust that covers the path. There have to be some places
that this path connects. Keep walking in either direction and you just
might get there. The path seems as endless as the mountainside you have
beside you. More mountainous terrain awaits you south and east.

Exits.Description: A little path takes you through the mountains.
A little path takes you through the mountains.

Rooms.Name: On a mountain path
Rooms.Description:
The path winds up and down, up and down, but it looks used. You see
the fine grain dust that cover the path. There have to be some places
that this path connects. Keep walking in either direction and you just
might get there. The path seems as endless as the mountainside you have
beside you. More mountainous terrain await you west and north.

Exits.Description: A little path takes you to the mountain.
A little path takes you through the mountains.

Rooms.Name: On a mountain path
Rooms.Description:
The whindling mountain path ends here or starts here depending on if
you came travelling down or from the south, shifting over into a set of
stairs. The stairs look really clean, either it is used a lot or
someone sacrifices a good deal of work and time to keep it clean.

Exits.Description: A little path takes you through the mountains.
A loooooooong stairwell.

Rooms.Name: A long stairwell in the mountains
Rooms.Description:
The steps are somewhat low to make climbing them easy. It is clearly
noticeably that you are in dwarven territory. The well tidied steps go
up and down from here. Below you the lower end of the stairs is visible.

Exits.Description: An even loooooooonger stairwell.
A loooooooong stairwell ends.

Rooms.Name: A long stairwell in the mountains
Rooms.Description:
The steps are somewhat low to make climbing them easy. It is clearly
noticeably that you are in dwarven territory. The well tidied steps go
up and down from here. Above you the upper end awaits your arrival.

Exits.Description: A loooooooong stairwell ends.
An even loooooooonger stairwell.

Rooms.Name: Top of some mountain stairs
Rooms.Description:
A fine little road surrounded by some bushes leads you between the top
of some stairs cut out directly from the mountain and something east of
here engulfed in some terrible greyish fog.

Exits.Description:
A big grey road goes towards the grey entrance of some huge grey
complex.
A loooooooong stairwell.

Rooms.Name: Following a road in the mountains
Rooms.Description:
The mountain road winds as it leads you through the mountainous
terrain. Make sure you do not slip a fall would be very disastrous. The
road goes north and west. Pick one or enjoy the view and the fresh air.

Exits.Description: You see little road trail off.
A little bushed road leads away.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Marvellous stone and sky make for a magnificent panorama for you to
enjoy.

Rooms.Name: Chute for walking guards
Rooms.Description: Takes them in to places between mill entrance and chasm 6554-6562

Rooms.Name: The Start of the Old Trail up the Mountains
Rooms.Description:
You are standing at the base of the Moria mountains. A half cleared
trail leads up the mountains to the north. To the south a trail leads
back to Midgaard. Far to the west you can see the river flowing into the
mountain and to the east you see the large forest of Namir. A large sign
has been placed on a pole here.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The sign reads
North, Old Trail to the Dwarven mines.
South, Trail to the city of Midgaard.

Rooms.Name: Old Trail up the Mountain
Rooms.Description:
You are on a half cleared mountain trail. You are walking between
high cliffs and large rocks. The trail makes its way upward to the north
and to the south it goes down to the base of the mountain.

Rooms.Name: Old Trail up the Mountain
Rooms.Description:
You are walking on a old trail up the mountain. Large rocks and
cliffs surround you on both sides. The trail continues up to the north 
and down to the south.

Rooms.Name: Old Trail up the Mountain
Rooms.Description:
You have almost reached the top of the mountain. To the south you see
the forest of Namir. If you look very closely to the south-west you can
see the city of Midgaard. The trail continues up to the north and down
to the south.

Rooms.Name: Old Trail up the Mountain
Rooms.Description:
You are walking on a trail going up the mountain. Further ahead the
trail makes a turn around a large cliff. If you walk north you will go
around this rock and if you walk south you will go down the mountain to
its base.

Rooms.Name: The Hidden Room
Rooms.Description:
In a small, dark space lit only by a cheery magical fire, a troop of
gnomes swap tales in a storytelling contest.  The smokeless fire has
burned the same logs for many long years, and the outside world seems
far away.  There is a magical quality about this room, and it seems easy
to forget that there IS a world outside this one.

Exits.Description: The rough-hewn planks seem to fit together poorly.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Many years ago, the group left their yak farm on the plateau to help
their friends the dwarves.  Iron ore production was down, and the gnomes
relied on the fine plow-heads made by the dwarves, so there was a bit of
self-interest as well.  Once the gnomes had created and installed a
system of pulleys to help harvest the ore, they retreated to this small
cottage for a story-telling competition, the prize to be possession of
an enormous jar of cookies.  They have been here ever since.  No gnome
can resist the lure of a good story.

Rooms.Name: The plateau
Rooms.Description:
Here the narrow path leads to a plateau. On the plateau the path divides in
one branch going north up the mountain and one going east up the mountain.
To the south the path goes down to the valley.

Exits.Description: The path continues.
Mountain trail

Rooms.Name: Narrow path up the mountain
Rooms.Description:
You are on a narrow path leading up a ragged mountain. To the south the path
makes its way to a plateau.

Exits.Description: The path continues up the mountain.

Rooms.Name: Narrow path at the middle of the mountain
Rooms.Description:
Standing on the middle of the mountain, you can easily see the city of 
Midgaard far to the south, and the top of the mountain is very near to the
north.

Exits.Description: The top of the mountain is easily seen from here.

Rooms.Name: Top of Mountain
Rooms.Description:
You are now on the top of the mountain. To the south you see a path leading
down the mountain. To the east and west you see entrances to what seems like
mines.

Exits.Description: An entrance to the mountain which seems to lead underground.
There is an entrance to the mountain.

Rooms.Name: Narrow Path
Rooms.Description:
This is a narrow path leading to the Dwarven Kingdom. It looks less
traveled than the others, and it is very creepy. The path opens up to the
south, and continues to the north.

Rooms.Name: Entrance to Mountain
Rooms.Description:
Here is an entrance to the mountain. The door looks very well built, and you
can hear noise coming from within.

Rooms.Name: Bend in Narrow Path
Rooms.Description:
This is a narrow path that bends to the east here. The trees hang over the
path, and it is very overgrown. The narrow path continues to the south and to
the east.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: They hang over the road in the most ominous of ways.

Rooms.Name: Narrow path
Rooms.Description: This path is very narrow, and it continues to the north and west.

Rooms.Name: Narrow north-south path
Rooms.Description:
This path leads to the north and south. To the north you can see a door, and
to the south the path continues.

Rooms.Name: Door to Kingdom
Rooms.Description:
Here the path turns to the west. You can see a door in front of you, and the
path continues to the west and south.

Rooms.Name: Path to the Castle
Rooms.Description:
You are on a path that will eventually lead to the castle. It continues
north to the castle, and there is a door on the southern wall.

Rooms.Name: Still on the path to the Castle
Rooms.Description:
You are still on the path to the castle, or back to the Dwarven village,
whichever way you wish to go. The path continues to the north and south.

Rooms.Name: Door to Castle
Rooms.Description:
Here there is a door to the castle to the east. The castle is elegantly
designed, and looks much like a roll of toilet paper standing on it's end.
There is a sign which says: ****************************************** *
WELCOME TO THE CASTLE OF STRANGELOVE * * Here, celibacy is uninvited *
******************************************

Rooms.Name: Inside the entrance
Rooms.Description:
Everything here is covered in soot and very grimy. The path continues to the
east and north, and there is a door to the west.

Exits.Description: The little underground path continues to the north.
The path leads outside the entrance.
This looks like an entrance to some type of store room.

Rooms.Name: Path
Rooms.Description:
You are on a path in the dwarven village which leads north to the shops and
south to the corner of the area.

Rooms.Name: Turn in road
Rooms.Description:
You are on a path that leads to a Hide & Tooth shop to the west, and the
path continues to the south.

Exits.Description: The Hide & Tooth shop is seen to the west.

Rooms.Name: Hide & Tooth Shop
Rooms.Description:
You are in the Hide & Tooth shop. Here you may buy the finest in Dwarven
weapons and armors. The path continues to the north and east.

Rooms.Name: Path to the north of shop
Rooms.Description:
You are on a path to the north of the Hide & Tooth shop. The path continues
to the north, and there is Granite Head's bakery to the west.

Rooms.Name: North of Shops
Rooms.Description:
Here the path bends to the east towards the barracks. To the south you can
see the shops.

Rooms.Name: Path by Hospital
Rooms.Description:
Here the path passes by the Hospital to the north. It continues to the east
to the barracks, and to the west.

Rooms.Name: Path next to barracks
Rooms.Description: Here the path continues west, and east to the barracks.

Rooms.Name: Entrance to barracks
Rooms.Description:
Here there is an entrance to the barracks to the south, and the path
continues to the west.

Rooms.Name: Guard House
Rooms.Description:
You are in the guard house to the west of the entrance to the castle. There
are nudie posters covering the walls.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: There is a wall poster of a nude Minne Pearl.

Rooms.Name: First Barrack room
Rooms.Description:
Here is the first of two main rooms of barracks. The barracks continue to
the south, and you can leave the room to the north.

Rooms.Name: Back of Barracks
Rooms.Description:
Here is the back of the dwarven barracks. There are rows of beds here, and
there is a stench that is unbearable.

Rooms.Name: Inside of Castle Strangelove
Rooms.Description:
You are just inside the castle. It is very tubular in shape, and it is very
featureless. There is a set of stairs that lead up, and the door leads out of
the castle to the west.

Rooms.Name: A store room
Rooms.Description:
There is a layer of dust on the floor at least 3 inches thick! It is
probable that not many people have been in here for many months.

Exits.Description: A lighted area that looks like a well worn path.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: After blowing all the dust off the floor, you notice a trapdoor!

Rooms.Name: Wine cellar
Rooms.Description:
This room smells like wine, and you can only assume it used to be a wine
cellar at one time.

Rooms.Name: Stairs in castle
Rooms.Description: The stairs continue to circle up and down here.

Rooms.Name: Stairs
Rooms.Description:
You are still circling around on the stairs. You are starting to get dizzy
from going around and around and around and around and around. The stairs
continue up and down.

Rooms.Name: Top of stairs
Rooms.Description:
You are at the top of the stairs in the castle. There is an exit to the
east, and the stairs lead down.

Rooms.Name: Queen's waiting room
Rooms.Description:
This is the Queen's waiting room. Here the men literally "wait" for the
queen. You've heard that the queen really likes to get to 'know' her people, in
the biblical sense. The queen's bedroom is to the north, and you can see stairs
to the west.

Rooms.Name: Bedroom
Rooms.Description:
This is the Queen's bedroom. The bed is all ruffled, and there is a stack of
dirty sheets piled in the corner. There is a ladder that leads down, out of the
castle, and you can leave the room to the south. There is a sign that says:
------------------------- | I'm busy right now, | | and don't know when | | Ill
be back, but if | | there is a key here | | take it and PLEASE, | | try to get
my birth | | control pills back! | | I've heard they can | | be found
somewhere, | | deep in the mines.. | -------------------------

Rooms.Name: North side of Castle Strangelove
Rooms.Description:
You are standing on the north side of Castle Strangelove. You notice that
you are no longer inside the mountain anymore either. Along the southern
horizon you see towering mountains. THIS AREA IS NOT OPEN SO GO BACK UP!

Rooms.Name: Hospital
Rooms.Description:
You are inside the Dwarven Hospital. It smells like rubbing alcohol, and
there is blood all over the walls.

Rooms.Name: Granite Head's Bakery
Rooms.Description:
The aroma coming from this room is astonishing. You can almost taste the
pastry's dissolving in your mouth.

Rooms.Name: Dark path
Rooms.Description:
This path is very well worn, and there is an entrance to the mines to the
east, while the path continues to the north and west.

Rooms.Name: Mine entrance
Rooms.Description:
The little path here leads down toward the mines, while the worn path
continues to the west.

Rooms.Name: Bottom of mineshaft
Rooms.Description:
You are at the bottom of the mineshaft. The air here is very sooty, and it
is very hard to breath. The mineshaft leads up and east.

Rooms.Name: Path in the mine
Rooms.Description:
You are deep inside the mine, and you feel very uncomfortable. The path
continues to the east, and leads to the mineshaft to the west.

Rooms.Name: Mine crossroad
Rooms.Description:
You are at a crossroad in the mine. There is a door to the north, and the
path continues to the south, east, and west.

Rooms.Name: Coal Room
Rooms.Description:
You are inside the storage area for the raw materials that are found down
here. The room is very unsturdy as the supports are very rickety.

Rooms.Name: Mine Maze
Rooms.Description:
You have entered the maze of the mines. To the east you can see some
inscriptions, and you can exit to the south.

Rooms.Name: Maze inscription
Rooms.Description:
You are inside the maze, but not far enough in that you could get lost.
There is an inscription on the wall which says: 1 3 2 4 N W N S This isn't too
tough, so don't take it so rough.

Rooms.Name: Maze
Rooms.Description: You are in a maze.

Rooms.Name: Maze
Rooms.Description: You are in a maze.

Rooms.Name: Maze
Rooms.Description: You are in a maze.

Rooms.Name: Mining equipment room
Rooms.Description:
This is the storage room for equipment used by the Dwarven miners. It is
very small, and you can tell that not many miners actually use any equipment.

Rooms.Name: Solved the Maze
Rooms.Description:
You have solved the maze. You can tell by the last few moves that there is
no way that a dumb worker could have figured that out. It seems pretty desolate
here. To the south is a bleak room. To the north, you see the maze. There is a
sign above the south exit: THOSE WHO ENTER, PLAN ON A TIMELY DEATH. (ESPECIALLY
IF YOU'RE LOYAL TO THE QUEEN)

Rooms.Name: The Mazekeeper's Room
Rooms.Description:
You have entered the Mazekeeper's room. There are pictures of the Queen with
darts thrown in it. Spray painted on the wall are things like 'the queen shall
suffer' and 'Catholics Rule'.

Rooms.Name: The Start of the Old Trail up the Mountains
Rooms.Description:
You are standing at the base of the Moria mountains. A half cleared trail
leads up the mountains to the north. To the south a trail leads back to
Midgaard. Far to the west you can see the river flowing into the mountain and
to the east you see the large forest of Namir. A large sign have been placed
on a pole here.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The sign reads
North, Old Trail to the Dwarven mines.
South, Trail to the city of Midgaard.

Rooms.Name: Old Trail up the Mountain
Rooms.Description:
You are on a half cleared mountain trail. You are walking between high 
cliffs and large rocks. The trail makes its way upward to the north and to the
south it goes down to the base of the mountain.

Rooms.Name: Old Trail up the Mountain
Rooms.Description:
You are walking on a old trail up the mountain. Large rocks and cliffs
surround you on both sides. The trail continues up to the north and down to
the south.

Rooms.Name: Old Trail up the Mountain
Rooms.Description:
You have almost reached the top of the mountain. To the south you see the
forest of Namir. If you look very closely to the south-west you can see the
city of Midgaard. The trail continues up to the north and down to the south.

Rooms.Name: Old Trail up the Mountain
Rooms.Description:
You are walking on a trail going up the mountain. Further ahead the trail
makes a turn around a large cliff. If you walk north you will go around this
rock and if you walk south you will go down the mountain to its base.

Mobs.Name: dwarf dwarven guard miner
Mobs.LongDescription: A dwarven guard shifts from foot to foot, bored.
Mobs.Description:
Perhaps the smartly golden yellow uniform laden with gold braid and
bright ribbons of honor is a point of pride with the guard, or perhaps
he simply takes his job quite seriously.  In either case, the uniform is
spotless, the beard neatly combed and braided, the boots spit-shined.
Mobs.ActionScript:
%%10 em snaps to attention.
;%5 em eyes you suspiciously.

Mobs.Name: Hagbard dwarf dwarven worker miner
Mobs.LongDescription: Fortunately for Hagbard the Helpless, Hermann the homely heals him.
Mobs.Description:
Hagbard the Helpless is not really helpless at all, of course, but he is
frequently hurt by the many hazards the miners face on a daily basis.
Somehow, fate has a way of finding him when there is a cave-in, noxious
gasses fill the tunnels or a boulder decides to roll off in search of a
dwarf to crush.
Mobs.ActionScript: %%10 em tugs at your sleeve, looking piteous.

Mobs.Name: dwarf angel mining
Mobs.LongDescription:
An angel servant of Kwazihuatl makes the world glow before your very
eyes.
Mobs.Description:
Mining is a hard and dangerous job.  Who needs a guardian angel more than
those who seek to rip the flesh from Mother Earth?  This little angel is
never seen, but he has the thick beard, thick calloused fingers and
stocky build of a veteran miner.  He wears the mark of Kwazihuatl, god of
dwarf miners.
Mobs.ActionScript: %%cast 3 miner

Mobs.Name: holgarth storekeeper
Mobs.LongDescription: Holgarth the Singing #wShopkeeper#Y waits for you to make up your mind.
Mobs.Description:
Holgarth likes to sing, especially in the interior caverns of the
mountain, where the acoustics are often unpredictable.  Since his last
aria deep underground was abruptly ended by the loud rumble of a
cave-in, his king has asked that he restrict his songs to soft croons.
Mobs.ActionScript: %%5 hum

Mobs.Name: baker
Mobs.LongDescription: Granite Head is known for bread hard as the iron dug from the mountain.
Mobs.Description:
Granite Head is a tall, strong dwarf wearing a large white apron.  He is
well-dusted with white flour, spices and ground rock.  As he is the only
baker in the area, the miners rely on him for their daily meals.  He
also furnishes the bar with their small list of edible fare.

Mobs.Name: lizard
Mobs.LongDescription: A giant cave lizard is foraging for food along the cavern floor.
Mobs.Description:
Godzilla?  No, just an overgrown cave lizard.  He thrives on the many
insects and small animals that dwell here under the mountain.  His cool,
dark green skin looks firm and spiky in places, and you can see the
muscles rippling beneath.  His long forked tongue whips out to sample
the air.

Mobs.Name: giant
Mobs.LongDescription: A giant is wandering around the mountainside, looking for food.
Mobs.Description:
The giant is about 18 feet tall, with arms of steel, and looks in
excellent physical condition.  It takes a lot to keep that small
mountain of muscle and flesh in peak condition, and so he's not too
picky about what (or who) he eats.

Mobs.Name: dwarven dwarf miner mineworker worker
Mobs.LongDescription: A dwarven mineworker whistles while he works.
Mobs.Description:
The mineworker is quite tired, but he enjoys the whistle of breath
through his mustache, and the way the whistle echoes throughout the
cavern.

Mobs.Name: dwarven mineleader dwarf mine leader miner
Mobs.LongDescription: The mine leader can out-dwarf any of his mineworkers.
Mobs.Description:
Out-dwarf?  He can out-drink the most bottomless of them.  With a dull
pick-axe and a played-out vein of ore he can outproduce the swiftest.
And when he combs out his luxuriant blond beard, you can see it's the
longest.  No wonder he's the leader!

Mobs.Name: doctor dwarf healer
Mobs.LongDescription: Amazingly, this dwarf is as barecheeked as a newborn (non-dwarf) babe.
Mobs.Description:
Very unusual - most likely unique among dwarves, this dwarf is smooth
cheeked and recently shaven.  He looks at you with an air of fatherly
concern, and when he fingers his beard-trimming shears you note the
twinkle in his merry brown eyes.
Mobs.ActionScript:
%%5 say Open wide!
;%5 say Take a deep breath!
;%5 say That beard is going to have to go, I'm afraid.
;%5 say Tsk! Tsk!

Mobs.Name: ill dwarf miner
Mobs.LongDescription: Hope what this dwarf's got isn't catching, whatever it is!
Mobs.Description:
With his pasty skin and wispy beard, it's clear this miner is not well.
Most dwarves would rather suffer their many illnesses than risk a visit
to this doctor, known for his large sets of beard-trimming shears and
razors.
Mobs.ActionScript:
%%10 sneeze;
%14 cough

Mobs.Name: ypeels miner sleepy dwarf
Mobs.LongDescription: Yawning loudly, the miner wonders why you're in his dream.
Mobs.Description:
With no daylight and no moonlight, time loses meaning and the miners
often sleep unusual hours.  This one has been asleep for about an hour,
and is convinced you are part of his nightmare.  Beware!
Mobs.ActionScript:
%%10 yawn;
%5 snore

Mobs.Name: dwarf sick miner
Mobs.LongDescription: Miraculously, the dwarf in the pool of blood on the floor still lives.
Mobs.Description:
Bleeding profusely from his many wounds, the dwarf awaits the doctor's
healing touch.  He must be desperate to be here, because the doctor is
known for his (*cringe*) shaving gear.
Mobs.ActionScript: %%10 bleed

Mobs.Name: offduty guard miner
Mobs.LongDescription: The guard sits with his feet propped up on the table in front of him.
Mobs.Description:
Bored by his companion's lies, yet secretly wanting to believe them, the
guard shares some lies of his own.  It's all part of a long-standing
game they play, seeing who can tell the most outrageous but unprovably
false tales.

Mobs.Name: offduty guard miner
Mobs.LongDescription: An offduty guard sits back, swapping lies with his buddies.
Mobs.Description:
Ale in hand, calculating look in his eye, the offduty guard tells his
buddies about all the giants he has killed, wenches he has seduced, and
secret veins of gold he has discovered.
Mobs.ActionScript:
%%8 say And then there was this mountain troll ... got 'im with me axe, I
did!
;%5 say Caught this little giant boy red handed, up to his ears in the
ale!
;%5 say 'ave you 'eard what they're usin' fer labor down at the mill?!

Mobs.Name: guard miner
Mobs.LongDescription: Glaring out at you from under his helmet, the guard looks fierce!
Mobs.Description:
Clearly you've wandered into a part of the mine where you shouldn't be.
There were no "VERBOTEN!" signs, nothing that actually SAID "off
limits", but from the look on this guard's face, you'd better go back
the way you came - and fast!
Mobs.ActionScript:
%%8 grumble
;%5 say I coulda been a sergeant by now if'n I'd worked guard duty up at
the mill.

Mobs.Name: guard miner
Mobs.LongDescription: The guard looks menacing in the full glory of his heavy chainmail.
Mobs.Description:
Dwarven chainmail protects the bulging biceps and massive thigh muscles
of the mining guard.  It's not clear what he's guarding against, or who,
but his size and his uniform are pretty awesome.
Mobs.ActionScript: %%8 spit

Mobs.Name: giant snake sssnake
Mobs.LongDescription: The giant sssnake looksss about for a ledge from which to hang.
Mobs.Description:
Hisssss!  Thissss sssnake can ssssee in the dark, ssssso watch out!  It
lookssss much to large to ssssettle for mere mice, indeed, it looksss
large enough to swallow a dwarf, whole.
Mobs.ActionScript:
%%8 em hissssssses.
;%6 em looks you over, looking for a nice juicy bare spot on your skin to
sink
his fangs.

Mobs.Name: queen Gwandolyn dwarven dwarf
Mobs.LongDescription: Queen Gwandolyn idly picks at her nose-wart, making it bleed.
Mobs.Description:
In truth, even the dragons could not abide Gwandolyn's rather nasty
temper.  They didn't bother to toast her, but they would much rather
not live near this perpetually cranky dwarf.  The mining dwarves
remain mellow, however, drenched in their marvelous ale.

Mobs.Name: king Kwathoum wide-bottom
Mobs.LongDescription: King Kwathoum the wide-bottomed wipes drops of ale from his beard.
Mobs.Description:
King Kwathoum the Wide-Bottomed son of Raktwein the Orc-Hunter is fairly
diminutive for a dwarf.  Far below the normal stature for his race, he
barely reaches shoulder height on his queen.  The dominant feature of
this little dwarf is his truly immense nose.  Point of pride for
Kwathoum, it looms out over his long, luxuriously golden beard which,
itself, curls merrily down towards his knees.
Mobs.ActionScript: %%6 tango queen;%8 daydream

Mobs.Name: sleep sleeping sleeper miner
Mobs.LongDescription: A miner sleeps sprawled out over his pallet on the mine floor.
Mobs.Description:
Impervious to rumblings deep in the belly of the mountain, loud snores
from other sleeping dwarves, and the odd, awe-full, noisome smells of
many unwashed bodies (and socks), the miner is so-o-o tired that he
sleeps deeply, dreaming, perhaps, of finding the hidden vein of gold in
this mountain.

Mobs.Name: egil dragon sleeping
Mobs.LongDescription: Let sleeping dragons lie.  (Old Dwarven Saying)
Mobs.Description:
Egil is a very very old dragon, centuries old, older than most other
dragons in this world.  He is the source and the keeper of dragon tales,
dragon history.  He is revered by other dragons.  The dwarves both fear
and respect him, and leave him in peace.  He is their totem, their
cave-god, lord of all beneath the surface of the earth.
Mobs.ActionScript: %%10 snore

Mobs.Name: shy lfuhsab dwarf miner
Mobs.LongDescription: One dwarf is hiding behind a metal fern wreathed in blue smoke.
Mobs.Description:
To enhance the ambiance in this little hole-in-the-(rock)-wall bar, the
management has spread about many plants.  Without sunshine, real plants
would die, so metal plants have taken their place.  This dwarf is
uncomfortable in the bar (nobody knows his name), and is shyly hiding
behind the metal fern.
Mobs.ActionScript: %%8 blush

Mobs.Name: yzeens dwarf miner
Mobs.LongDescription: A bright red nose and droopy eyes warn you to stay clear of this miner.
Mobs.Description:
Wiping his painfully red nose on the rough woolen sleeve of his tunic,
the miner wonders idly if he is allergic to the mine dust, the smoke
from his pipe, or simply life.  He is strong and in good spirits,
though, and not a dwarf to trifle with!
Mobs.ActionScript:
%%10 sneeze
;%8 em rubs a nice clean hankerchief against his reddened, dripping nose.

Mobs.Name: yppah dwarf gronlgrg gr#<oe>nlgrg
Mobs.LongDescription: Singing, Gr#<oe>nlgrg works at separating rock from mountain.
Mobs.Description:
His fellow dwarves duck and work up quick excuses when they see
Gr#<oe>nlgrg coming.  His persistent cheeriness, smiles and ready
laughter are like a dull pickaxe scraping along smooth rock to the
others.  It is hard for even a dwarf to be mean spirited to
Gr#<oe>nlgrg, mostly because he is impervious to such behavior.
Mobs.ActionScript: %%8 sing

Mobs.Name: yepdo dwarf miner
Mobs.LongDescription: The dwarf sits in the dark, wondering why he can't see.
Mobs.Description:
While he's not very clever for a dwarf, still, his lack of brilliance
generally doesn't lead him into trouble.  Indeed, he has a fool's own
luck, just not the intelligence to take advantage of it.
Mobs.ActionScript: %%8 twitch

Mobs.Name: miner dwarf
Mobs.LongDescription: The mighty dwarf enjoys reaping iron ore from the heart of the mountain.
Mobs.Description:
Putting his massive back into each swing of his pickaxe, the hardworking
dwarf gets into a steady rhythm reminiscent of a heartbeat as he chips
away at the heart of the mountain.  As with his brethren, this dwarf was
born to the life, born to carve out his domain beneath the surface of
the earth.

Mobs.Name: miner handsome dwarf
Mobs.LongDescription: The very handsome dwarf spends a moment to stroke his beard.
Mobs.Description:
He is average height for a dwarf, about 4', or about 1.25 m (as
the European dwarves would measure him).  His hair is lushly thick and
the golden color of the ale he loves.  His body hair is also thick, so
much that his eyebrows seem to join over his nose, forming a single
ridge of hair.  His beard is likewise thick and long, and full of odd
objects, insects and bugs that have yet to be combed away.
Mobs.ActionScript:
%%7 admire handsome;
%5 holdhand handsome

Mobs.Name: giant Thorvald
Mobs.LongDescription: Thorvald yawns, accidently swallowing a small bird.
Mobs.Description:
Thorvald doesn't notice.  He's a bit tired, and a bit hungover, and not
too bright, in any case.  The bird was flying nearby and got sucked in
by Thorvald's mighty yawn.  Thorvald may notice a bit of a fluttering in
his stomach.  But probably not.
Mobs.ActionScript: %%5 say chirp!

Mobs.Name: Hermann cod
Mobs.LongDescription: Hermann the Homely has helped Hagbard heal his wounds.
Mobs.Description:
Hermann would have liked to be THE healer, but a relative of Gwandolyn
the queen was given the post.  He is a kind dwarf with a gentle, if
exceedingly homely face.  The dwarves believe that the devil sickness is
frightened away by Hermann's homeliness.  Perhaps it is so.

Mobs.Name: death
Mobs.LongDescription: Death haunts the subterranean regions of the mine.
Mobs.Description:
A miner's life is often cut short by the many things that may go wrong,
from poisonous gas, to a cave in, a slip of the axe or the fire of an
awakened cave-dragon.  Death is always with them, hidden in the dark
underground passages.
Mobs.ActionScript:
%%5 em looks you over craftily, measuring the days you have left to your
 pathetic life.
;%8 em tells you, "I hear Harold the Undertaker has a good deal on now.
Maybe you should take advantage of it and save your family some money."
;%8 em silently sharpens his scythe, waiting for your hourglass to empty.

Mobs.Name: Magnus giant
Mobs.LongDescription: Magnus the Merciless flexes his magnificent muscles.
Mobs.Description:
Magnus the Merciless crushes all before him.  Standing tall, even for a
giant, he spends some months out of each year lifting huge iron bars at
the dwarven steel mill.  Besides the plentiful food, the mill gives him
an opportunity to develop and tone his beautiful musculature.
Mobs.ActionScript:
%%5 em admires his magnificent biceps.
;%5 flex
;%5 sing magnus

Mobs.Name: Gr#<oe>tben grotben giant
Mobs.LongDescription: Dragging his leg, Gr#<oe>tben tries to finish his meal while on patrol.
Mobs.Description:
Grog, greasy pig meat, grainy wholemeal bread, Gr#<oe>tben gobbles it
all down while gimping along on patrol.  Gr#<oe>tben is on the lookout
for grog-thieves and other greedy souls.
Mobs.ActionScript:
%%1 yell #rFee #cFie #gFoobar #mFumble#W
;%8 em picks a small nit out of his body hair and sticks it in his
sandwich.

Mobs.Name: Uzhumer ypmurg dwarf
Mobs.LongDescription: Uzhumer the Cranky growls, "Get back where you belong, dirtwalker."
Mobs.Description:
Uzhumer the Unhumorous ... Uzhumer the Cranky ... Uzhumer who would eat
iron ore before he would say thing remotely cheerful.  A dwarf of middle
years, his thick, wildly wavy black hair has grown a small halo of gray.
His face is deeply lined, all lines pointing down of course, from his
perpetual glower.  Still, he is a good friend for those who can endure
his eternal pessimism.
Mobs.ActionScript:
%%5 grumble
;%4 say What do you think you're looking at?
;%5 say Get back where you belong, dirtwalker.
;%5 glare
;%3 raspberry

Mobs.Name: gnome Nell
Mobs.LongDescription: Cmdr Nell, Chief of Gnomish Spy Operations, hunts for her cookie stash.
Mobs.Description:
Nell is a very commanding little gnome (other gnomes call her bossy).
She takes her job as Chief of Gnomish Spy Operations (GSO) and Overseer
of Ballooning (OB) very seriously.  She and Kith are on a mission to
Discover the Lost Gnomes.  A small party of gnomes left GnomeHome some
(few hundred) years ago never to be seen again.  They were to assist
(for a princely fee) the dwarves in their mining operations, about which
they had an intense (and intensely gnomish) curiosity.
Mobs.ActionScript: %%5 say  WHO FORGOT THE COOKIES???

Mobs.Name: gnome Kith
Mobs.LongDescription: Kith's in charge of Watching Over Nell, who often thinks she's Xena.
Mobs.Description:
Kith is one of the Sensible Gnomes (yes, there are a few, mostly from a
Sensible Gnome village just northeast of Midgaard).  It is his duty to
see that when Nell starts playing Warrior Princess, she comes to no
harm.  He is also actively searching for The Lost Gnomes, who left the
yak farm where they were brought up to seek adventure in the wide world,
and to Help the Dwarves.

Mobs.Name: gnome Martha
Mobs.LongDescription: Martha, Junior Gnomish Spy, waits for her turn with the spyglass.
Mobs.Description:
From their landing place high in a Giant Tree, the gnomes can see much
of the mountain.  They have brought a spyglass, and Martha is itching to
get her delicate gnomish fingers on it.  The gnome who discovers the
Lost Gnomes will be famous in Gnomish History.  Martha is small and
delicate, even for a gnome.  Her skin is smooth, soft, the color of
aging parchment.  She is the youngest of the Gnomish Spy Group.
Mobs.ActionScript:
%%3drop stick
;%3 rem stick
;%1 get stick
%5 say Lemme see! Lemme see! Have you found them??

Mobs.Name: Bint gnome
Mobs.LongDescription: Bint listens, enraptured, as her friends frighten her with stories.
Mobs.Description:
Bint sits in the dark at the back of the small hut, listening in
fascination as her friends weave tales of horror and mystery, brave
adventures of derring-do and narrow escapes through rifts in the fabric
of time.  She has long since forgotten WHY she is hidden away here.
Mobs.ActionScript: %%5em munches away on a chocolate cookie.

Mobs.Name: Ernie
Mobs.LongDescription: Ernie became lost in his own story, a tale of 4 gnomes underground.
Mobs.Description:
Ernie, Magnificent Storyteller, is part of the famous Legend of the
Lost Gnomes.  He is a gnome of many years, and his fair hair now grows
in small wisps atop his head.  His clothing is covered in several years
of accumulated dust.  His current tale, one of the adventures of 4
gnomes living under a great mountain, is one of his best.  Then again,
it's also all quite true.
Mobs.ActionScript:
%%8 say ... and then, one of the dwarves told them the Legend of the
Great
Cookie Jar ...

Mobs.Name: Genna gnome lost
Mobs.LongDescription: Genna looks hungrily at the cookie jar, which holds the remaining stash.
Mobs.Description:
Genna agreed to a Gnomish Story Swap as a prelude to a Gnomish Cookie
Feast, but the Story Swap, although fascinating, is taking
f-o-r-e-v-e-r, and she is #rhungry#N!  She is a very chubby little
gnome, covered with a hundred years or so of accumulated dust (which she
doesn't notice nor, if she did, would she mind).  Her turn at
storytelling is next, and she is thinking of a story involving 4 little
gnomes who perish of hunger in the middle of a storytelling fest!
Mobs.ActionScript: %%5 em blushes as her stomach growls loudly.

Mobs.Name: Squish lost gnome
Mobs.LongDescription: Squish shivers in fear at the tale of gnomish ghosts haunting.
Mobs.Description:
The stories are deliciously scary, spooky and frightening.  Squish
likes best stories about ancient, evil gnomes coming back as ghosts,
haunting the living.  Although, truth be told, he's never known a truly
evil gnome, he's fully prepared to believe they exist.  Squish was
but a lad of 173 when his expedition left on a Great Adventure in the
Underground Land of the Dwarves.  He fully expects to be part of a Great
Gnomish Legend himself one day!
Mobs.ActionScript: %%8 em shivers, moving a little closer to the other gnomes.

Mobs.Name: termite
Mobs.LongDescription: A giant termite flies at you spitting acid, fangs ready for your throat.
Mobs.Description:
This is a termite like you've never seen before!  Termites should be
small and easily quashed.  This one is as big as you are, with the
armature and weaponry of the fierce insect that he is.  Got any bug
spray?
Mobs.ActionScript: %%5 say I never met a tree I didn't like ... to bite!

Mobs.Name: Hrugnar giant
Mobs.LongDescription: Hrugnar swallows his potent grog more easily than his buddies' tales.
Mobs.Description:
After all, Hrugnar has spun some of the same tales himself.  Hrugnar is
a larger than average, well respected giant, with shoulder-length thick
blond hair that he wears tied back with a dragon-leather thong.  He
loves to go stomping with his fellow giants, and brags about the many
dragons he has slain.
Mobs.ActionScript: %%5em picks a really big louse out of his beard and flicks it away.

Mobs.Name: Olaf giant
Mobs.LongDescription: Olaf shouts up to Astrid, "C'mon, sugar-pie, I won't be gone long!"
Mobs.Description:
Olaf is large, even for a giant, with a big, hairy barrel chest, a large
grog-belly, and thighs like tree trunks.  He loves to go out stompin
with his friends, which basically means getting roaring drunk and
creating as much havoc as possible in Stanneg, Tynstri and any of the
other small villages they stumble into.  Astrid tries hard to make a
good husband and a good provider out of him, but the raw material she
has to work with is lacking a LOT.
Mobs.ActionScript:
%%5 belch
;%8 say Awww, Astrid, angel-face, I've just #wgotta#N go stompin' with
the guys!

Mobs.Name: Lodur lefty
Mobs.LongDescription: Lodur the Left Handed looks for someone to loot.
Mobs.Description:
Lodur the sLy, "Lefty Lodur" as the wanted posters call him.  A very
sinister looking man, he hides among the large lilies of the valley,
preying on lone travelers, leering at them from behind large lilies,
lunging out at them, looting them, then leaving them leaking blood.
Mobs.ActionScript: %%8 em deftly slips his hand into your backpack and grabs some gold.

Mobs.Name: Astrid
Mobs.LongDescription: Astrid yells down to Olaf, "Don't you sugar-pie me, you little worm!"
Mobs.Description:
Well, I suppose only another giant could call Olaf "little".  Astrid is
a small, feminine giantess with lush curves in all the right places (at
least, Olaf thinks so).  Her pale blond hair is kept firmly braided and
wound around her head like a coronet.  Her eyes are the deep blue of a
summer sky, as Olaf tells her when he's been out stomping.
Mobs.ActionScript:
%%5 em yells down to Olaf, "You get up off your lazy hairy bottom, Olaf
 and get up here and DO something about that boy of yours!"
;%5 em yells down at the "boys", "You just take yourselves off to the
 Stubbies Steel Mill and find yourselves an #whonest#W job and stop
 all that #wstompin!#N
;%8 em yells to Olaf, "You stomp any more dirt in here and #wI'll stomp
 all over you, I will!!#N"

Mobs.Name: Gullveig giant girl
Mobs.LongDescription: Gullveig has looked EVERYWHERE for her Nelly doll, so it must be hiding.
Mobs.Description:
Gullveig looks much like a younger version of her mother, Astrid.  She
is small, fair, with long blond braids that end, usually, in a dirty
ribbon.  Her deep blue eyes look out at you with interest from a face
with very regular features, cool creamy-white skin and a very determined
expression.  She radiates confidence in herself and her abilities to
make the world grant her desires.
Mobs.ActionScript:
%%5em says, "Nelly!  Where are you Nelly?  C'mere Nelly!"
;%5 pout
;%5 sulk

Mobs.Name: Nelly doll
Mobs.LongDescription: The Nelly doll looks furtively out from under Astrid's bed.
Mobs.Description:
The doll is, indeed, hiding from Gullveig.  And she hopes fervently that
Gullveig will NEVER find her.  Indeed, she's been working hard on a
"forgetting" spell so Gullveig will forget she ever HAD a Nelly doll.
Nelly is dressed as the real Nelly does for her Mind Bogglingly
Magnificent Mindslayer act.  Her rainbow cape hides many magic
treasures.  Although she is a doll, she is (hopefully WAS) the toy of a
giant girl, and so she is quite as large as an average human, larger
than Nelly the Gnome. Nelly's  brief flame of fame led every little girl
to want a Nelly doll.
Mobs.ActionScript:
%%5 em peeks nervously out from under the quilt on the bed.
;%5 em tells one of the Lost Argyles to stay lost.

Mobs.Name: guard Gunnar giant
Mobs.LongDescription: It's not clear whether Gunnar is guarding the gate or his grog.
Mobs.Description:
Gunnar's favorite position is rocking back on the back two legs of his
chair, feet propped up on the desk, grog in hand, staring up at his
favorite pinup girl (Helga).  The road sees little activity beyond the
occasional lost tourist (quickly dispatched for a snack) or a small
expedition of giants out for a good stomp.  This suits Gunnar's
personality quite well.
Mobs.ActionScript:
%%5 em gulps down another tankard of grog.
;%5 spit
;%5 sing

Mobs.Name: Ymer
Mobs.LongDescription: Ymer the Stout lumbers about trying to stay upright after the grogfest.
Mobs.Description:
Of course there is always something to celebrate, and this time Ymer
really tyed one on.  He's not too sure how much grog he swallowed,
although he has a vague memory of heading down to the cellar for another
barrel and being startled there by a tiny person wearing spectacles.
Not that gnomes or dwarves are unknown to him, but they rarely make it
into the stronghold without being eaten.
Mobs.ActionScript:
%%5 hiccup
;%5 em puts his head in his hands and moans.

Mobs.Name: Gunhild
Mobs.LongDescription: Redhaired Gunhild stays busy sweeping the gallery floor.
Mobs.Description:
Gunhild's deep red hair tells you something about her temper.  The giant
children are rather naughty about leaving their things over the floor,
and Gunhild sweeps them right off the floor, through the railing that
runs around the U shaped floor and onto the heads of the giants below.
This is very distressing to the children.  The giants, when they are in
the hall below, don't seem to notice.
Mobs.ActionScript:
%%8 em shakes her broom at you threateningly.
;%8 mutters, "Children should be kept outside, where they belong!"
;%15 spank Stanley

Mobs.Name: Stanley
Mobs.LongDescription: Stanley shouts "Stop!", seeing small sweets slide slowly away.
Mobs.Description:
Stanley is a small (for a giant) and very nasty little boy.  His mother
Astrid is constantly attempting to placate him with sweets, but he
continues to whine.  He is a VERY fat little boy, with rotten teeth and
breath (from all the sweets) and a tendency to throw very loud temper
tantrums.  His father is very proud of Stanley's lungs.  If Gunhild
continues to sweep Stanley's sweets off the floor, and if Astrid
succeeds in keeping Olaf home, then Olaf will undoubtedly get to hear a
LOT more of his son's powerful voice.
Mobs.ActionScript: %%2 fart;%10 tantrum;%3 innocent

Mobs.Name: Ulfar
Mobs.LongDescription: Idly polishing his mighty war-axe, Ulfar glares down at you.
Mobs.Description:
Ulfar is one of the mightiest of the giants who live at this stronghold.
He is probably the only one who combines both intelligence and size.
Unfortunately he also believes bathing is a conspiracy foisted by
smaller races upon the mighty, and he steadfastly refuses to
participate.  Of course, the other giants are not big fans of bathing
either, but they occasionally DO swim - or at least fall into large
bodies of water.
Mobs.ActionScript: %%5 em idly picks at his lice.

Mobs.Name: rugrat
Mobs.LongDescription: All whiskers and long tail, the rugrat watches the world walk by.
Mobs.Description:
All grey and brown fur (and dust), the rugrats love to roll around in
the dust beneath the bed, playing with the small toys that they filch
from Stanley.  They are clever little rugrats, blending into the carpet
when they need to hide, but sneaking out when nobody is looking to
steal candy and small treasures.
Mobs.ActionScript: %%3 rub

Mobs.Name: argyle argy sock
Mobs.LongDescription: Argyle the Sock isn't really lost, he's just on vacation.
Mobs.Description:
Let's face it.  Being a sock is NOT the World's Best Job!  You encase
something whose odor is the source of endless jokes, and you become
yourself, seeped in that odor.  You are constantly trod upon in the hot
humid darkness inside a shoe.  You never get to SEE anything beyond the
inside of a drawer, but have to rely on the shoe's description of the
world.  Once used, you're flung aside to be tramped on until you are
thrown into a large vat of water and drowned, only to go through the
entire cycle again.  Argy and his brother have escaped this terrible
fate by the simple strategem of separating.  Only one of them had to
hide.
Mobs.ActionScript: %%10 twitch

Mobs.Name: dog hound wardog
Mobs.LongDescription: The vicious wardog is dreaming of tearing prey limb from limb.
Mobs.Description:
One of Ulfar's favorites, the dog (Ulfar calls him "Dog") stands half
again as tall as a normal human (if there is such a thing).  Ulfar says
if he had a half dozen dogs like this one, the giants would Rule the
World instead of just using it for their plaything.
Mobs.ActionScript: %%2 growl

Mobs.Name: bnarkl dwarf spy
Mobs.LongDescription: Bnarkl silently observes, making mental notes of all he sees.
Mobs.Description:
Bnarkl is the Ultimate Dwarven Spy, sent to keep an eye on the giants
via the fake barrel of grog in the cellar of their stronghold. Bnarkl's
beard and mustache are well-trimmed and well-waxed.  He is slender for a
dwarf, but as a spy, he is continually needing to get out of "tight
spots". He is not sure why he was told to spy on the giants, but he
reports back on their grog supplies and occasionally makes a small hole
in one of the kegs.  The giants (like everyone else) buy their ale from
the dwarves.
Mobs.ActionScript: %%4 peer;%5 pace

Mobs.Name: Biff brewmaster
Mobs.LongDescription: Brewmaster Biff glares sternly at you. "You can buy your ale next door."
Mobs.Description:
Ooops!  You've stepped into the private (and very busy) domain of Master
BrewMaster Biff the Fat.  Gnomish hops and a secret, ancient dwarven
recipe are used to brew the best and most potent ale known to dwarf (or
gnome or man).  Grog, a byproduct of the process and considered by the
dwarves to be not-worth-bothering-with, is sold to the giants who live
northeast of here.
Mobs.ActionScript: %%5 glare;%5 threaten

Mobs.Name: gnomish gnome farmer
Mobs.LongDescription: The farmer polishes the twirly horn of his favorite yak.
Mobs.Description:
A small group of communal gnomes farms the rich pastures near the
dwarven mountains.  They provide the dwarves with flour, hops, and
advice on the steel mill machinery, and the dwarves give them the finest
ploughs and steel wool (for polishing the yak horns) that exist in this
world.
Mobs.ActionScript: %%8 praise yak;%5 admire yak

Mobs.Name: yak
Mobs.LongDescription: The magnificently hairy yak likes to yak it up with fellow yaks.
Mobs.Description:
At 2 m. (6'6") high at the shoulder, covered with thick, meaty muscles
and thick, wildly growing hair, with two long, curving horns that stick
w-a-y out in front of him, the yak believes himself to be a very sexy
beast.  With a small horde of awestruck gnomes to cater to his every
whim, brush his hair till it shines, feed him raspberries and celery,
and polish his rainbow horns, life seems pretty fine to the yak and his
herd.
Mobs.ActionScript: %%7 twitch

Mobs.Name: Brunhilde giant B
Mobs.LongDescription: Brunhilde leans on the railing, trading insults with the giants below.
Mobs.Description:
Giant courtship rituals are bizarre, aren't they?  Brunhilde ("B" to her
friends) is a large giantess, with broad shoulders, strong arms, and a
will of iron.  Her carrot-red hair falls in two long braids down to her
waist.  She has been flirting with many of the male giants for years
now in this fashion, but life near Astrid and Olaf has convinced her
never to marry.
Mobs.ActionScript:
%%3 flirt;%5 chuckle
;%5 say Ha! Not all of you is so giant, Ulfar!
;%5 say I've seen more hair on a chicken, Bjarke!

Mobs.Name: Bjarke giant
Mobs.LongDescription: Bjarke thumps his friend hard on his back, nearly toppling him.
Mobs.Description:
A giant of great good cheer, Bjarke is the result of a life with no
fear.  He is a giant among giants, tall and powerful with rippling
muscles and a constitution strong as the iron the dwarves labor so hard
to reap from their beloved underground.  Because he has known no fear,
and even misfortune has never dared cross his path, Bjarke is easy-going
and rarely cranky.  Given his size, it might be a good idea to keep him
that way.
Mobs.ActionScript:
%%8 guffaw
%3 em laughs heartily.

Mobs.Name: Jilly gnome
Mobs.LongDescription: Jilly rolls out the cookie dough to cut into fantastical shapes.
Mobs.Description:
Cook(ie Baker) Jilly loves baking pepparkakor cookies for the little
(and not-so-little) gnomes at Christmastime - and most other times.  The
little gnomes help her cut out the gingerbread-gnomes and trees and
snowflakes and yaks and moons and stars and anything else they can
imagine.  Once baked, the ones that are not immediately gobbled are
decorated with Jilly's special white icing.

Mobs.Name: Thobias
Mobs.LongDescription: Thobias pauses in the path, puffing on his briar pipe.
Mobs.Description:
Tobias has been busily negotiating the sale of the tobacco the dwarves
love so much in exchange for some fine ale brewed especially for the
halflings.  He is a middle-sized halfling of middle years, round and
chubby, with a special vest and jacket to hold his travelling pipes.

Mobs.Name: gnomish sleeper gnome
Mobs.LongDescription: Shhh! Don't wake the sleepers!  They've had a long day.
Mobs.Description:
A farmer's day is long and hard, even if you're a gnomish yak farmer.
During the long spring and summer, crops are planted to feed the yaks
through the winter.  The farm is mostly self-sufficient, so food and
material for clothing must be grown and then canned or processed.
Mobs.ActionScript: %%4 snore

Mobs.Name: Razzl
Mobs.LongDescription: Razzl grabs a basket and heads off towards the berry fields.
Mobs.Description:
Razzl is a small, neatly turned out gnome, with a bright pink dress, a
long white apron and wide-brimmed straw hat trimmed with a bright pink
ribbon.  Razzl is headed off to pick strawberries, which Jilly will use
to make jam.  Yum!  Extra strawberries will go to the yaks, who actually
purr when fed strawberries and cream.

Mobs.Name: Dazzl
Mobs.LongDescription: Dazzl trudges off to pick raspberries, well-stained basket in hand.
Mobs.Description:
Dazzl would rather be skinny dipping in the creek, but the yaks and the
gnomes both thrive on the raspberries, so she's off to fill her basket
before it gets dark.  Dazzl, Razzl's twin sister, is about average
height for a gnome, which is to say, not so very tall.  She has a bounce
in her step (when she's not headed for the raspberry patch) and a
twinkle in her eye.

Mobs.Name: Znugl
Mobs.LongDescription: Znugl barks playfully, announcing your arrival.
Mobs.Description:
Znugl is one of the many yak herding dogs kept and trained by the yak
farming gnomes.  She is about mid-thigh height for an adult gnome, but
due to her training she believes strongly she is the head yak,
responsible for keeping the rest of the yaks in order. She is a
cheerful, playful, noisy part of the farm.
Mobs.ActionScript: %%9 bark

Mobs.Name: gnome explorer
Mobs.LongDescription: The Gnomish explorer is out to discover the world.  Wherever it is.
Mobs.Description:
Having packed up all that he can into his small backpack, dressed warmly
in yak's wool trousers and vest, with a small leather cap, the explorer
has set out to discover the world.  Not many travellers make it to his
off-the-beaten-track yak farm, but enough to stir his innate gnomish
curiosity.  The bespectacled gnome walks boldly, hoping to go Where No
Gnome has Gone Before.

Mobs.Name: runner Thialfi
Mobs.LongDescription: Thialfi races past you in a blur of motion.
Mobs.Description:
A young blond lad with a passion for goat meat, Thialfi is the fastest
man alive.  He has a runner's build, lean with long legs. Thialfi and
his sister Roskva were presents to Thor, when Thor was a guest at their
cottage.  Thialfi disobeyed Thor, and it was a narrow thing, whether he
would be killed on the spot or not.  Thor has a rather nasty temper!

Mobs.Name: Gupfo
Mobs.LongDescription: Gupfo gathers the gardening gnomes, giving good instructions.
Mobs.Description:
Gupfo is Chief of Gnomish Gardeners, in charge of Growing Green things.
Needless to say, he especially loves glossy eggplant, geraniums,
greengage pears and giant squash.
Mobs.ActionScript:
%%8 daydream
;%1 say Geeeee ...

Mobs.Name: farmer gnomish gnome
Mobs.LongDescription: Farming the fertile plateau fascinates the gnomish farmer.
Mobs.Description:
Well, most EVERYTHING fascinates the curious gnomes.  The farmer has
been hardened by the active life of waking at dawn, working with the
land and with his small herd of yaks and other farm animals.  His skin
is dark from the sun and quite tough and leathery.
Mobs.ActionScript: %%5 say Fine field of fenugreek there!

Mobs.Name: chicken
Mobs.LongDescription: The chicken flaps her wings wildly, as if she is about to lay an egg.
Mobs.Description:
This is an ordinary, dumber-than-celery chicken with dirty white
feathers.  Her life has been spared thus far, although she has yet to
produce her first egg.

Mobs.Name: rooster
Mobs.LongDescription: The rooster struts, master of all he surveys.
Mobs.Description:
Or at least, master of all the hens he surveys.  Which is all he really
cares about.  And since he is the only rooster around, it's likely he
will remain Chief Rooster.  Unless he becomes Chief Fried Chicken some
evening when one of the War Gnomes gets tired of his boasting.
Mobs.ActionScript: %%5 strut

Mobs.Name: miner
Mobs.LongDescription: The miner is looking forward to spending some of his gold on ale.
Mobs.Description:
Back and arms rippling with muscles from years of heavy labor under the
crust of the earth, encrusted himself, head to toe, with a bit of that
earth, this miner is looking forward to a night drinking ale and talking
with his buddies.

Mobs.Name: sleeping guard
Mobs.LongDescription: Shhh! This guard was out on patrol all night and must sleep now!
Mobs.Description:
Well, okay, it's hard to say when you're underground whether you are up
all day or all night.  The dwarf comes from a family which proudly
traces their ancestry back to Ratootl the Big-Eared Goblin Muncher.  He
definitely has the ears.

Mobs.Name: guard
Mobs.LongDescription: The guard struggles to get the cave-grit off his boots before sleep.
Mobs.Description:
The Chief Officer Dwarf has a fetish for well-shined boots, so the
dwarves try to at least get most of the dust from their boots before
they sleep.  No polishing materials are provided, so they simply rely on
the ready supply of discarded socks and underwear littering the floor.

Mobs.Name: Scruffy wardog dog
Mobs.LongDescription: Scruffy the vicious wardog is out looking for a wild adventure.
Mobs.Description:
And if she gets caught by Ulfar she'll be dog-stew in no time.  Scruffy
sneaked out the green door when Gr#<oe>tben left to go on patrol, and
she has no intention of going back soon.  Tail high, sniffing the
breeze, she's one happy wardog.
Mobs.ActionScript:
%%5 em lifts up her chin and sniffs delicately at the air.;%5 em looks
around for some nice dead animal to roll in.

Mobs.Name: Brandy wardog dog
Mobs.LongDescription: Brandy the escapee wardog races along the road, head and tail held high.
Mobs.Description:
Brandy escaped the giants' stronghold where Ulfar was trying hard to
turn her into a vicious war dog.  With tail held high and waving like a
war banner, she sniffs delightedly at all the wonderful scents.
Mobs.ActionScript: %%5 growl

Mobs.Name: corndog dog
Mobs.LongDescription: The corndog snaps at you as you brush past the corn.
Mobs.Description:
The corndog is a deep, golden brown and kind of chubby from a life of
determined indolence.  He is extremely large, about as tall as the
average adult male gnome, and his size alone generally is enough
deterrent to keep hands (and beaks) off the corn.

%%5 bark
;%5 growl
;%5 say Stay out of the corn!
;%5 emote is a Dog of the Corn.

Mobs.Name: lab tech gnome
Mobs.LongDescription: The lab tech hurries about taking samples and making notes.
Mobs.Description:
The lab technician's longish pointed ears poke out from his wispy brown
hair.  He wears a dirty white cotton lab coat with plenty of pockets to
hold his notepads and pens and samples of plants.  The lab tech is
putting himself through College of Gnome by his work here at PARC.

Mobs.Name: wentworth crazy
Mobs.LongDescription: Crazy Wentworth wildly waves a smoking beaker in your direction.
Mobs.Description:
You may have no concrete idea what is in the beaker that Crazy
Wentworth, the mad scientist is waving about, but you should know enough
to stay out of his way.  Wentworth has gone off the deep end ... too
many hours here and too many samples of some of his new fungi.

Mobs.Name: farmer gnome gnomish
Mobs.LongDescription: The #ggnome#Y farmer tenderly cares for his sunshine loving plants.
Mobs.Description:
The farmer's face is weathered a deep brown but is amazingly free of
lines.  The warm radiant heat and the healthy joy of the sunflowers have
given him a relaxed strength beyond what one might expect of a small
gnome.
Mobs.ActionScript: %%3 em smiles brightly at the plant.;%3 say Good morning, Sunshine!

Mobs.Name: sunflower plant sun
Mobs.LongDescription: The sunflower lifts its face to the sun, reflecting radiance onto you.
Mobs.Description:
Bright yellow petals fringe the huge deep brown face of the giant
sunflower plant.  The sunflower absorbs massive amounts of the sun's
rays and reflects them back out at the world.

Mobs.Name: dragon onyx
Mobs.LongDescription: #GThe sculptor captured this dragon in a moment of hot fury.#N
Mobs.Description:
This sculpture is so lifelike you can almost feel the heat of the
dragonflame shooting from the dragon's mouth.  The dragon is reared up
high, front paws clawing the air, long dragontail forming a sinuous
curve behind.

Mobs.Name: viking giant boy
Mobs.LongDescription: Late at night the giant boys sneak ale from dwarf storage.
Mobs.Description:
Once their folks are asleep (in their beds or in their grog), the boys
sneak out and follow the secret passageway down to where King Kwathoum
keeps his Private Reserve.
Mobs.ActionScript: %%5 burp

Mobs.Name: j noble lady
Mobs.LongDescription: Lady J from the court of King Welmar is touring the countryside.
Mobs.Description:
In a fancy coach, accompanied by a retinue of servants, Lady J. has
decided to take a rest from the intrigues of court life and enjoy a
visit to the country.  At least, that is what people back at court were
told.  But many rumors are afloat about her ... Where is she headed?  A
secret rendez-vous with someone?  Who?

Mobs.Name: guard court Reginald
Mobs.LongDescription: Reginald's rings flash in the light as he drums his fingers restlessly.
Mobs.Description:
All the nobles of the Court of Welmar travel with an escort, of course.
While he is a well-loved ruler, still every kingdom has its malcontents
and there are assassins known to be lurking along well-travelled routes.
The guards are chosen to match in height and build, and they are all
about 6' tall and quite muscular.  The ladies are all quite fond of
them, but they are only fond of each other.
Mobs.ActionScript: %%5 em drums a little beat with his fingers.

Mobs.Name: dresser
Mobs.LongDescription: Lady J's personal dresser is as neat as a pin.
Mobs.Description:
Brought along to take care of Lady J's priceless silk dresses and keep
her jewelery in order, the dresser works long, hard hours, but takes
immense pride in her lady's appearance. Lady J counts on her dresser to
handle the small details of matching slippers to gloves, packing and
unpacking.
Mobs.ActionScript: %%5 frown

Mobs.Name: servant
Mobs.LongDescription: King Welmar always sends Lady J off with a large staff of servants.
Mobs.Description:
Anxious that Lady J be cared for as she would if she had remained at
court, good King Welmar insists that she bring a number of the castle
staff with her when she travels.  This small gnome will server several
purposes during the trip, from brushing the dirt from a walkway before
Lady J steps on it to running ahead to find an inn for the night.

Mobs.Name: chef
Mobs.LongDescription: Lady J's private chef sharpens his knife as he looks for local edibles.
Mobs.Description:
"Eet must be fresh!  Fresh for ze lady!" screams the chef, who has
dreams of being famous one day.  He forces the guards to stop frequently
so that he may gather fresh herbs in fields that they pass, or orders
them to kill some innocent animal for fresh meat.  He is a small, hefty
man with a large girth, missing teeth, and very bad breath.

%%5 em hopes nobody is looking as he sneaks another one of Jilly's
cookies out of his pack.

Mobs.Name: juggler
Mobs.LongDescription: A juggler lightly tosses apples into the air.
Mobs.Description:
The juggler's empty hat lies on the ground in front of him, ready for
your tossed coins.  He is a light and agile fellow, quick witted as well
as quick fingered.

%%5 beg
;%5 say A few coins in the hat, may your piglets all be fat!
;%5 say Tis good luck to give in to that urge to drop some pennies in.

Mobs.Name: tobacco trader halfling
Mobs.LongDescription: The halfling trader heads off to turn his wagon of tobacco into gold.
Mobs.Description:
Hobbit tobacco is known the world over.  This halfling has a full wagon
of well aged, golden tobacco.  He will sell it or trade it to the
dwarves for fine metal work, to the gnomes for perhaps some fresh yak
butter and he will probably try to avoid the giant settlement.

%%5 say What'll it be, friend?  A little hobbit tobacco to ease your

Mobs.Name: assassin
Mobs.LongDescription: The assassin waits in hiding for a wealthy member of the court to pass.
Mobs.Description:
The long track connecting the kingdom of King Welmar with the Kingdom of
the Dwarves is one of few well formed paths in this world, and so it is
a good bet that if she waits long enough, a clever assassin may capture
a bit of the wealth that travels this road.

%%8 em eyes you quietly from his hiding place in the shadows.
;%8 em looks you over, wondering how much loot you are carrying.

Mobs.Name: root
Mobs.LongDescription: A hairy root gropes for you in the dark.
Mobs.Description:
Growing from who-knows-what kind of plant, this root is sentient, and it
senses some nice juicy prey ... YOU!  Small fingerlike projections cover
its tentacles and they are reaching for you ...
Mobs.ActionScript: %%5 grope

Mobs.Name: myconoid
Mobs.LongDescription: The myconoid fungi love the damp, dark mustiness of the cellar.
Mobs.Description:
You've seen this fungi growing in cellars and dark, damp places all over
the world.  They are gross, fuzzy little beings, making disgusting
little noises and smelling vaguely of laundry that someone forgot to
hang out to dry.

Mobs.Name: goat
Mobs.LongDescription: The long horned mountain goat jumps nimbly over rocks.
Mobs.Description:
This goat is one of a small herd that is still looking for the sweet
meadow grass on the other side of a bridge.  For this reason they seem
always to be hopping around, on the move.

%%5 em hops about from rock to rock.
;%5 em gently headbutts you, prodding you with his small horns.

Mobs.Name: trader halfling
Mobs.LongDescription: Carrying a burden of dwarven-made pots and shovels, the trader is weary.
Mobs.Description:
The halfling trader always dreads this part of his journey, although he
is by nature cheerful.  At least during the uphill journey his burden is
light ... tobacco, yak butter and milk, corn and other food supplies.
The metal products from the dwarven kingdom are quite heavy though, and
the burden is difficult.

Mobs.Name: viking giant boy
Mobs.LongDescription: The giant boy swallows ale a barrel at a time.
Mobs.Description:
Once their folks are asleep (in their beds or in their grog), the boys
sneak out and follow the secret passageway down to where King Kwathoum
